summary: One source-backed restriction: every supported inner polynomial lacks a cubic term, so canonical example e-181 cannot be replayed. Tested outputs, grader cases, rendering and packaging passed; no affected stored record was demonstrated.

source_analysis.skill: Differentiate a polynomial raised to a positive integer power using the chain rule; evaluate slopes and form tangent lines in the documented higher-difficulty families.
reasoning_steps: Identify inner polynomial g and outer power n.
Compute n*g^(n-1) and g prime independently, multiply and substitute.
For slope questions evaluate at the supplied abscissa; for tangent questions use the slope and point.
invariants: One polynomial inner function and positive integer outer power; no radicals or transcendental outer functions.
All dependent expressions and coordinates derive from the same polynomial, power and target.
Radio options are distinct with exactly one derivative/slope/tangent answer.
Blank grading accepts algebraically equivalent polynomials.
permitted_variations: Vary nonzero coefficients and signs, constants, outer exponent, source-supported polynomial degrees and variable names within comparable workload.
Vary evaluation abscissa and consequent ordinate, slope sign and zero/nonzero outcomes where valid.
Reorder inner terms or answer choices without changing mathematical correctness. Correct position and distractor size/order are incidental.
Relevant coefficient/exponent/target changes must update answer and solution; irrelevant term ordering must preserve answer.

source_replay.details: All 12 practice questions replay their mathematics and complete radio banks. q-340690 correctly omits an incorrect historical blank alternative; q-48625 needs inferred key/solution. Two derivative prompts normalize whitespace around the blank. Canonical e-181 cannot replay its quartic-plus-cubic inner polynomial.

math.details: Independently differentiated displayed prompts for 146 records: keys correct, radio alternatives distinct, one correct choice. Point coordinates checked exactly; representative worked solutions inspected. This does not certify the missing canonical family.

variety.details: 120 stratified samples vary coefficients, signs, powers, points and bank ranks. However, the canonical second-term degree is suppressed by every constructor. All 36 sampled easy records and all 5 runner records survive captured delivery; selection limits are documented.

scope.details: Observed outputs retain polynomial-power differentiation, source-supported slope/tangent tasks, response types and difficulty workloads. The separate coverage restriction is not scope drift.

grading.details: Native learner grader passed 78 acceptance and 106 rejection checks, including expanded/factored blank equivalents, wrong polynomials, all radio options and stale answers after relevant changes.

rendering.details: Actual UI rendered 20 records without reported errors. Ten representative screenshots inspected for notation, controls, worked solutions and counterfactual propagation.

packaging.details: Exact runtime dependency versions match manifest. Relocated package output matches original for seed 99173/count 5. Boundary rejection and deterministic replay checked; original package file hashes unchanged.

decision_variation.details: Relevant coefficient, power and point changes propagate through prompts, solutions and grading; term-order changes preserve the answer. Conditional shortcut probes found no perfect predictor in sampled runtime templates. Nevertheless the source-supported second inner term cannot change from linear to cubic; its derivative role is unjustifiably fixed.

findings.description: The polynomial constructors exclude the KP canonical example (3x^4+x^3)^5. The quartic branch always uses a*x^4+b*x, so its second inner-derivative term is always constant rather than allowing the source-required 3*x^2. Every other supported branch also has zero cubic coefficient. This is a generator-domain omission, not an incorrect answer in the five easy batch records.

findings.requested_change: Retain the quartic-plus-linear family and add source-grounded support for a cubic second inner term, either as an explicit term-degree slot or a canonical-derived family. Derive prompt, inner derivative, answer bank and solution from that term structure. Replay e-181 exactly and add a controlled linear-versus-cubic regression. Preserve existing difficulty separation; no database repair is requested.
